entities.summary:
Apple Inc. is an American multinational technology company founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne in a garage in Los Altos, California. It designs, develops, and sells consumer electronics, computer software, and online services, becoming the world's first company to reach a $1 trillion market capitalization in 2018.

Apple transformed personal computing with the Apple II in 1977 and the Macintosh in 1984, introducing the graphical user interface to mass consumers. The company's near-bankruptcy in 1997 was reversed when Jobs returned, launching the iMac, iPod, iTunes, iPhone (2007), and iPad — a product roadmap that revolutionized mobile computing and digital media consumption worldwide.

The iPhone fundamentally reshaped telecommunications, social interaction, and the global economy, spawning an app ecosystem worth hundreds of billions annually. Apple's design-first philosophy, vertical integration of hardware and software, and obsessive secrecy became a widely imitated business model. By 2023, Apple had surpassed $3 trillion in market capitalization, cementing its status as the most valuable company in history.
